record.paper_title: Modeling social resilience: Questions, answers, open problems
record.original_question: How can one explain and model why some social organizations thrive and enhance their core capabilities when faced with a crisis while other social organizations fail, where a social organization is a formal or informal group of interrelated individuals pursuing a collective goal and embedded in an environment? A usable answer should account for the organization's vulnerability or susceptibility to disruptions, its anticipation, foresight, or situational awareness for those vulnerabilities, and its adaptive capacity, flexibility, or fluidity in mitigating vulnerabilities or responding to disruptions.

artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open modeling problem in the literature on social resilience. No general mathematical framework simultaneously incorporating vulnerability, anticipation, and adaptive capacity and predicting thriving vs. failure of social organizations under crisis appears to have been established; existing approaches remain conceptual or domain-specific.

status_evidence.title: Modeling social resilience: Questions, answers, open problems
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly identified as an open question on organizational resilience modeling.
